newsitem.title: INDIA: Bose Corp to sell public venue products in India.
newsitem.headline: Bose Corp to sell public venue products in India.

text.p: U.S. audio product maker Bose Corporation will focus on selling high quality sound systems designed for public venues in India and later launch its home products, its president said on Wednesday.

"What we have decided to do is to focus on the applications of quality sound that will take place in public venues," Sherwin Greenblatt, president of the Massachusetts-based company, told Reuters in an interview in the Indian capital.
"We are initially focusing on introducing and making our products available in a broad range of public venues," he said.

Bose Corporation, founded by Amar Gopal Bose, a professor of electrical engineering at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), is globally known for its loudspeakers, music systems and high-quality sound systems in public places.
The privately-held company Bose Corporation has annual sales of $700 million, a company statement said.
The company received approval from India's Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) to set up a wholly-owned subsidiary, Bose Corporation India Private Limited, in 1995.
"For the present we are not worried about the manufacture (in India). We are worried about developing the marketplace first," Greenblatt said.
He said that the company would target auditoriums, stadiums, cinema halls, restaurants and stores to sell quality sound systems.
"This will give us an opportunity to learn more of the details of how to do business in India," he added. "It will give our products a visibility to a wide range of population."
He did not divulge any detail on the investment and financial plans of the company.
Bose Corporation would launch its home audio products at a later date, he said. The company was also looking at the vast Indian car audio market, officials said.
They said that there was no established distribution network for selling high quality sound products in India, making it difficult to market products.
Greenblatt said the company would develop infrastructure, provide software training and offer expertise to design quality sound products.
"Bose engineers will also offer their expertise in acoustics to Indian businesses and students through educational seminars and software training," the company statement said.
The company would provide maintenance and after-sales service for all its products.
Bose Corporation has also introduced its new Auditioner audio demonstration system in India.
"This system allows people to listen to the sound system before they are actually installed, either in existing buildings or those yet to be constructed," the statement said.
Greenblatt said that Bose Corporation looking at India from a long-term perspective.
"By making this commitment to do business in India, we are here to stay, as long as it takes, as hard it is. We will be successful here," he said.
Greenblatt said he hoped in five years India would become the fastest growing market in Asia for Bose Corporation.
